newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek cash rates, short fx forwards firm in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Greek cash rates, short fx forwards firm in late trade.

text.p: Greek money rates were slightly up and forex forwards were trading narrowly with an upward bias in the short-end of the yield curve with market players preparing for Monday's FRN auction.
"Depos are somewhat higher and forex forwards have firmed 10 basis points in short periods," said a trader at a foreign bank. "The market is bracing for Monday's FRN auction."
Traders agreed the auction will be succesful and the average price will be around par but there were conflicting views as to how much the auction interested foreign parties.
Some bankers said there was strong interest from abroad for the FRNs but others said the interest was negligible and it was up to local banks to sweep the floaters.
Greece will auction 250 billion drachmas of seven-year floaters with the first coupon set at 14 percent on Monday, October 21.
The spread is held constant at 150 basis points but the benchmark 12-month T-bill is slashed by 20 basis points to 12.50 percent.

The treasury reserves the right to accept non-competitive bids up to 30 percent of the auctioned amount, it said. It also reserves the right not to accept all or some of the competitive bids that will be submitted.
It reserves the right to accept competitive bids over the 250 billion drachma amount if non-competitive bids do not suffice to cover the 30 percent allotment.
The mark was quoted at 156.32/37 drachmas from Friday's 156.300 fix, the dollar at 240.83/93 drachmas from 241.010 and the Ecu at 300.44/54 from 300.350 drachmas.
"Nothing spectacular happened at the fixing," said a forex bank trader.
